items.d: PROJECT NUMBER: UT NP ARCH 100(2) PROJECT NAME: Bridges on Delicate Arch Road PROJECT DESCRIPTION: Delicate Arch Road (DAR) is within Arches National Park (Park) and provides access to Delicate Arch. DAR is a functional class 1 roadway (Principal Park Road) and is heavily traveled by visitors and often congested during periods with moderate-to-high levels of visitation. DAR crosses three low-gradient ephemeral washes (Salt Valley Wash, Salt Wash, and Winter Camp Wash) near their confluence in the Salt Wash Basin downstream of Wolfe Ranch. Culverts installed during original road construction in the mid-1990s and during subsequent upgrades are inadequate to allow unobstructed stream flow and sediment transport downstream. items.d: 1. Strategic Purpose: The Department of the Air Force, through the Air Force Test Center (AFTC) and Arnold Engineering Development Complex (AEDC), announces the establishment of the AEDC Velocity Alliance. This strategic consortium-based initiative is established under the authority of 10 U.S.C. § 4022 to accelerate the modernization of national test infrastructure in direct support of next-generation defense systems and key National Defense Strategy objectives. The objective is to establish a pre-qualified industrial base to execute a multi-billion dollar portfolio of complex engineering and construction projects. items.t: USCGC MORRO BAY (WTGB-108) — Fuel Oil Tanks and Bilge Cleaning and Inspection
items.d: The U.S. Coast Guard has a requirement for a qualified contractor to furnish all labor, supervision, materials, equipment, vacuum trucks, and hoses to perform fuel oil tank and bilge cleaning services aboard the USCGC MORRO BAY (WTGB-108) in Cleveland, OH. Bilge Cleaning: Vacuum offload approximately 2,500 gallons of mixed fluid (used engine oil, fuel, and bilge water). Thoroughly wash and degrease bilges to meet USCG-provided Marine Chemist gas-free/safe-for-hot-work inspection standards. Fuel Oil (F/O) Tank Cleaning & Fuel Disposal: Pump low-suction residue and dispose of approximately 11,500 gallons of contaminated Marine Gas Oil (MGO) / diesel fuel. Clean all internal tank surfaces free of residual fuel, sludge, biological growth, and foreign matter. items.t: Lower Brule North Shoreline Stabilization And Ecosystem Restoration, Element 2
items.d: The project is located along the right descending bank of Lake Sharpe near the Lower Brule, SD town site. Lower Brule North Element 2 includes a 100-foot-wide riparian planting bench, a gravel maintenance path along the entire reach, a riprap revetment to protect the shoreline and island from erosion, and the creation of a 200-by-1,500-foot island constructed in water up to three feet deep. The sheltered open water area between the island and the shoreline will develop into approximately 5.17 acres of emergent wetland, and this will also create approximately 32 acres of riparian habitat. Related tasks include earth moving, grading, bank shaping, rock installation, water management, fill, and topsoil placement.

items.t: Post Quantum Cryptography (PQC) Readiness and Validation Status
items.d: https://feedback.gsa.gov/jfe/form/SV_3t6dNlgkS4Vg6iy Federal agencies are preparing for the transition from cryptographic algorithms that may be vulnerable to future quantum computing attacks to quantum-resistant cryptographic algorithms standardized by the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST). Public key cryptographic algorithms (i.e. asymmetric cryptography) currently used across Federal information systems, products and services — including Rivest-Shamir-Adleman (RSA), elliptic curve Diffie-Hellman(ECDH), elliptic curve digital signature algorithms (ECDSA), and related mechanisms — will be vulnerable to a future cryptanalytically relevant quantum computer (CRQC). As a result, Federal agencies are expected to identify, prioritize, and migrate quantum-vulnerable cryptographic systems to approved post-quantum cryptographic algorithms. items.t: Air Force Contract Augmentation Program (AFCAP) VI
items.d: The 772nd Enterprise Sourcing Squadron (772 ESS/PKD) is issuing this solicitation for the Air Force Contract Augmentation Program VI (AFCAP VI). This is a Multiple-Award Indefinite-Delivery/Indefinite-Quantity (IDIQ) contract designed to provide rapid, global contingency planning, logistics, and emergency construction capabilities to the Department of the Air Force, other DoD components, and Federal agencies. The AFCAP serves as a responsive, global force multiplier for commanders and Government agencies, supporting contingencies both within the contiguous United States (CONUS) and outside the contiguous United States (OCONUS).The AFCAP supports United States (U.S.) national interests and security objectives by providing rapid-response capabilities for contingency planning, deployment, training/equipping of forces, emergency/contingency construction, logistics/commodities, and services.

items.t: Rosebud Lift Station Construction
items.d: The existing lift station has been in place since the early 1990s. Since its creation the hospital anticipates increased expansion in the emergency department, added on Tribal programs (dialysis, detox, Tribal Health Administration Building), added on 19 more quarters units, and is anticipating adding an additional 23 quarters units. The existing pumps are facing replacement every 1-2 years due to the unanticipated growth, but due to the growth we need to consider increasing the capacity of the wet well. In addition to switching from standard submersible pumps to chopper pumps to accommodate the random objects that get flushed into the system. In July both pumps ended up failing and they had to not only replace the pumps but pay for sewage disposal to circumvent overflow. A separate project is in the works to begin remediating/replacing damaged sewer mains due to inflow and infiltration.
